auto_updater: Move AwaitReboot logic to separate call. Quick provisioning path was erroneously expecting PostCheckCrOSUpdate to await for reboot, while in the non-quick provisioning cases this was being done prior to that call. This resulted in some race conditions and a few attempts to work around it incorrectly. Now, quick provisioning can just call AwaitReboot which will ensure that the DUT has rebooted before doing any other provisioning. BUG=chromium:812949 TEST=unittests, autotest/contrib/loadtest.py CQ-DEPEND=CL:931937 Change-Id: I10360b52892d15cc8b8177a26b25997b807ff4e9 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/932362 Commit-Ready: David Riley <davidriley@chromium.org> Tested-by: David Riley <davidriley@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Xixuan Wu <xixuan@chromium.org>

quick-provision: Await reboot before doing post check. Quick provisioning path was erroneously expecting PostCheckCrOSUpdate to await for reboot, while in the non-quick provisioning cases this was being done prior to that call. Now, quick provisioning can just call AwaitReboot which will ensure that the DUT has rebooted before doing any other provisioning. Add secilc to target-chromium-os-sdk. secilc is used to to compile SELinux intermediate language into SELinux binary policy. Currently, all SELinux policy lives under Android, ChromeOS build process simply copy it into ChromeOS filesystem. This adds development burden when updating ChromeOS policies. Developers needs to update Android tree, and then bump arc container version in ChromeOS in order to update ChromeOS-related SELinux policy. Introducing secilc allows ChromeOS to build overall binary policy by combining Android policies and ChromeOS policy at ChromeOS build time. And bump EAPI to 5. TEST=emerge BUG=b:69139821 Change-Id: I787f99e73ac5866480ecd756a8bc5a71d065b3d3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/928181 Commit-Ready: Qijiang Fan <fqj@google.com> Tested-by: Qijiang Fan <fqj@google.com> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kenny Root <kroot@google.com>

Forced AU at OOBE with interruptions. This test interrupts the forced update at OOBE by 1. Rebooting 2. Pulling the network for a couple of minutes 3. Suspend/Resume the device. We want to ensure the device can continue with the update no matter what end users do to the DUT. The test team manually performs these steps during every new device FSI. This test will remove the need for any more manual forced update at OOBE testing.
